conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Percolation
style.description: A white enamel board of glass sight-pipes, brass cross fittings and red-lever valves in a square grid, a trough of blue water along the top and a dry trough along the bottom. Valves click open in a seeded random order; open pipes are tinted by cluster on the enamel behind them; water fills only what it can reach from the top. An incremental union-find finds the exact valve that first joins top to bottom; when it turns, water runs the newly joined cluster down to the bottom trough. Bright, front-lit, clean diagram look.
motion: Every valve has one turn time from percolate.js; its lever swings 90 degrees (outBack) from across the pipe to along it.
Water is an earliest-arrival flood from the top trough over open pipes: each pipe fills from the end the water reaches, at a fixed time per pipe.
Open pipes not yet reached by water are tinted by cluster (a pastel band on the enamel); merged clusters cross-fade to the larger one's colour.
Camera: locked holds joined by short eased moves (no drift): top half, whole board, close-up on the deciding valve, pull back.

beats.label: Now it runs end to end

notes.mechanism: percolate.js: 16 x 8 joints, 264 valved pipes (13 rows of vertical pipes incl. both trough rows, 12 rows of horizontal). Seeded opening order; incremental union-find gives the exact pipe that first joins the top trough to the bottom one; pipes before it open in beats 1-3, it opens alone in beat 4, later ones never open. Water = earliest-arrival flood from the top trough over open pipes (B is a sink).
notes.sound: one click per 1/20 s bin of valve turns (gain ~ sqrt(count)); bubbles per bin of pipes starting to fill; pad bed released before beat 4 (silence), one loud clack + thud for the deciding valve, a riser landing as water reaches the bottom trough, chime + rumble there, a brighter pad under beat 5.
